thread:
Max: :rotating_light: APAC-c (apac-c) scheduler backlog hitting 70% for gpu-infer nodes, and we're seeing NAT egress failures to cloud-provider causing long tail errors. Need to steer ~30% traffic to NA for 45m while we scale and fix NAT. @oncall can we do TTL-based steer?
Anya: I see the autoscaler backoff alerts + pending instance provisioning delays. Runbook suggests GSLB/route adjustments. What endpoints are highest QPS?
Max: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings are the hot ones. Combined they account for ~82% of tokens in APAC right now.
Jia: Prefer a TTL-steer so we don't break client pinning. My plan: canary 10% -> 30% over 5m, TTL 45m, then observe. Use routectl to plan/apply. Example:```
routectl plan --scope global \n  --match path_prefix=/v1/generate --from region=apac --change weight=-10% --to region=na --change weight=+10% --ttl 300
routectl apply --id <plan-id>
```
Start with 10% for 3m, check queues, then push to 30%.
Lucas: NA spare capacity is ~40% for these models (measured last 5m), but cross-region egress cost will go up (~$0.02/token estimate). Do we accept the cost hit? Also watch for KV cache cold starts in NA.
Priya: Suggest enabling model-variant fallback in route policy to use a quantized variant in NA if we see latency spikes. Also enable short-lived retries (2s) in the edge config.
Max: ok running canary now. Planning command:```
routectl plan --scope global --match path_prefix=/v1/generate --from region=apac --change weight=-10% --to region=na --change weight=+10% --ttl 300 --note "apac-c scheduler backlog"
routectl apply --plan 8421
```
deploy-bot: Plan 8421 applied by Max. Rolling change: apac -10% -> na +10% (paths: /v1/generate,/v1/embeddings).
infra-bot: Alert suppressed: apac-c scheduler-backlog (muted for 10m) as part of active mitigation.
Anya: metrics dashboard shows immediate drop in apac tail-latency, queue depth down from 70% -> 40% after 90s. Good sign. Move to 30%?
Jia: Proceed but do incremental step: next plan to +20% (total +30).```
routectl plan --scope global --match path_prefix=/v1/generate --from region=apac --change weight=-20% --to region=na --change weight=+20% --ttl 2700
routectl apply --plan 8424
```
Max: applied plan 8424 -> target shift 30%.
deploy-bot: Plan 8424 applied by Max.
Lucas: NA latency stable, no cache meltdown, CPU on NA nodes up but within safe limits. Cost watch: egress tracked, so finance pinged.
Priya: NAT fix is in progress (cloud ticket 9821) — ETA ~25m. If the cloud provisioning finishes earlier we can start reversing steer with a short TTL.
Jia: Monitoring: keep eye on request success rate, p50/p95, and pod spinups. If NA CPU > 80% for 5m, abort and rollback.
Max: noted. I'll set an automated rollback job if NA CPU crosses thresholds.
(20m later)
Max: backlog now 10%, NAT ticket updated: partial recovery. I'm going to start a gradual return: -15% from NA back to APAC over 10m.
Jia: plan/apply:```
routectl plan --scope global --match path_prefix=/v1/generate --from region=na --change weight=-15% --to region=apac --change weight=+15% --ttl 600
routectl apply --plan 8430
```
deploy-bot: Plan 8430 applied by Max.
Anya: metrics show apac queue back to normal, tail latency stable. Re-enable alerts.
infra-bot: apac-c scheduler-backlog alert resolved.
Lucas: quick postmortem note: provisioning backoff + NAT egress flaps caused backlog; mitigation via TTL-steer costed extra egress but preserved SLOs. Recommend follow-ups: improve autoscaler backoff visibility, add NAT health probes, and pre-warm NA model cache for future cross-region steers.
Priya: +1 on pre-warm. Also propose a cost guardrail to limit cross-region egress % per hour without explicit approval.
Max: thanks team — closing the thread. Will open a short RFC for pre-warm + cost guardrails. :thumbsup:
